data.standardized_narrative: Antares Syndicate 1274 experienced an overall strengthening of prior year reserves by $113.131 million in 2021. This adverse development was primarily driven by the strengthening of reserves on older years of account, particularly for Professional Indemnity, Management & Transactional Liability, Contractors liability, and Hull classes from 2018 and prior underwriting years. The report also notes that COVID-19 impacted the prior year by $29 million, and reserves related to the pandemic were reviewed following a Supreme Court ruling on business interruption test cases. While some releases on more recent years were observed, the net effect was a strengthening.
raw_causal_phrases: strengthening of the prior year reserves on the older years of account, partially offset by releases in the more recent years
COVID-19 impacted the prior year by $29m adding 6% to the combined ratio
Syndicate was required to strengthen its 2018 and prior year of account reserves primarily in its Professional Indemnity, Management & Transactional Liability, Contractors liability and Hull classes
The deterioration comprises net claims including the change in claims incurred but not reported ('IBNR')

Following the Supreme Courts final judgement on the FCA's business interruption test case, which substantially allowed the FCA's appeal on behalf of policy holders, the COVID-19 reserves held by the Syndicate were reviewed in light of the updated court ruling and found to be appropriate.
data.data_quality_notes: The narrative on page 25 explicitly states a net deterioration of $13.653 million for prior year claims outstanding. However, the gross prior year development of $113.131 million was calculated from the gross claims development triangle on page 36, as per instructions to prioritize gross figures from triangles when narrative provides only net. The Motor line of business shows a negative gross premium written for 2021, which is unusual but reported as per the document.
